quotes.text: You might think this is a survey tool and it's really a pipe for answers. Forms is the starting point of a bigger process, since the answers it collects can flow straight into Excel.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes Forms from a simple survey tool into the entry point of an automated process.

quotes.text: Branching only moves forward. A question can send someone to a later question or to the end of the form, and it can never send them backward.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the one branching rule that trips up almost every new Forms author.

quotes.text: The effort pays for itself because a short form that only asks what's relevant gets finished, and a long form full of questions that don't apply gets abandoned halfway.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear, practical argument for using branching to keep forms short and relevant.

quotes.text: Here, the phrase export to Excel makes people picture a one time copy, a frozen snapshot they'll have to redo next week. The live workbook is the opposite of that because it keeps itself current while you touch nothing at all.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clears up the common misunderstanding between a live Excel workbook and a one-time export.

quotes.text: A form is the front door. Excel is where the answers settle, and Power Automate is what acts on them. You don't have to learn all of Microsoft in one go.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes how Forms, Excel and Power Automate work together as one chain.

chapters.title: Sharing the form and collecting answers
Automating the follow-up with Power Automate

takeaways: Microsoft Forms is included with Microsoft 365 and free Microsoft accounts and builds surveys, polls and self-grading quizzes in the browser without any setup.
Branching keeps forms short and relevant, but branches can only point forward, and Likert statements each count toward the two-hundred-question limit.
Opening results in Excel creates a live workbook, and a Power Automate flow triggered by a new response can handle approvals, notifications and logging automatically.
hook: Chasing survey answers by hand is slow, and the numbers go stale fast. This episode is for Microsoft 365 users, team leads and trainers who want to collect feedback, sign-ups or quiz results without a developer. You will learn how to build a form, use branching and quiz mode, send answers live into Excel and let Power Automate handle the follow-up.
